KuroganeOS 7.0.0-dev — Iron Shield / Driver & Device Expansion candidate

Iron Shield broadens real hardware coverage without changing the generic
network, storage, input, audio, UI or application contracts established by the
5.x portability work and 6.0 Core Steel.

Current 7.0 implementation:
- Intel Gigabit Ethernet family detection now covers the legacy 82540EM
  (8086:100E) and the E1000e-class 82574L (8086:10D3);
- both Intel NIC models continue to use the same bounded NetworkInterface
  contract consumed by DHCP, IPv4, TCP/TLS and Kurogane Web;
- E1000e keeps the existing legacy descriptor-ring ownership rules, dedicated
  DMA pages, reset/link validation and polling-safe fallback when MSI delivery
  cannot be retained;
- the shared QEMU smoke harness can instantiate e1000e explicitly;
- host regression validates PCI model classification and rejects unrelated
  Intel/non-Intel device IDs;
- a dedicated 7.0 Intel GbE gate requires real DHCP and gateway ICMP on both
  QEMU e1000 and e1000e devices;
- PCI power-management foundation validates PM capabilities and bounded
  D0/D1/D2/D3hot transitions, rejects D3hot while Bus Master DMA is enabled,
  verifies state writes and never replays the write-one-to-clear PME Status bit.

Qualified baseline carried forward:
KuroganeOS 6.0.0-dev Core Steel is qualified at exact source SHA
717e003b34d47c81495e8ac5c580ae57c5fb16b3. Scheduler 2.0, four-vCPU SMP,
Ring-3 execution on APs, preemption, Red Flux login/desktop and mouse-launched
Kurogane Web passed the exact-SHA Core Steel closeout.

Qualification boundary:
7.0 is an active development candidate until an exact Iron Shield candidate
passes its dedicated driver/device matrix. The first Intel GbE slice does not
claim RTL8111/8168, USB hub, device-power-management or broad physical-machine
qualification yet. Oracle VirtualBox, VMware and physical Intel/AMD systems
remain external validation targets unless explicitly tested.
